# Mileage {#sec-dd-mileage}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
by_year <- read_coverage("coverage_by_year")
by_year$share_mileage <- by_year$n_mileage / by_year$n_on_road
by_year$share_legit <- by_year$n_legit_mileage / by_year$n_mileage
by_year$share_odometer <- by_year$n_odometer_est / by_year$n_on_road
yr <- function(y, col) fmt_pct(by_year[[col]][by_year$year == y], 0)
mc <- read_pipeline("outputs", "quality", "mileage_checks.csv")
```

## Overview

The MOT test records the odometer reading, and the difference between two
tests gives the distance driven between them. The annualisation spreads that
distance over the calendar years between the tests to give an annual mileage
for each year. @sec-sources-linkage explains how the annual figures are
made, and @sec-mot-test what the MOT records.

- **`mileage_YYYY`** is the number of miles driven in year YYYY, from
  `r min(by_year$year)` to `r max(by_year$year)`.
- **`legit_mileage_YYYY`** is `TRUE` if that mileage is judged plausible.
  Filter on it for most analyses: the implausible values include odometer
  errors and readings typed in wrongly.
- **`total_mileage`** is the sum of the annual mileages over all years. It is
  0 for a vehicle with no recorded mileage, and decides `scope_mileage`
  (@sec-dd-identifiers).
- **`odometer_est_YYYY`** is the annualisation's estimate of the odometer
  reading in year YYYY, carried through unchanged. The pipeline does not
  use it: some estimates exceed 1,000,000 miles and some fall from one year to
  the next. It is in the maximal table only.

The pipeline takes the annual mileages as supplied (methodology,
[section 2](../../reports/methodology.md#input-data)), and summarises them in
the mileage tables
([section 8](../../reports/methodology.md#stage-6-mileage-summaries);
@sec-aggregate-tables). The table is wide, with one mileage column per year:
@sec-examples-code shows how to reshape it to one row per vehicle per year.

::: {.callout-important title="Mileage needs a test at each end"}
An annual mileage can only be calculated between two MOT tests, so a vehicle
has none before its first test or after its last, and the most recent years
are incomplete because many vehicles have not yet had their next test
(@sec-pitfalls).
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-mileage
#| tbl-cap: "Mileage columns."
dict_table("mileage")
```

## Coverage

The mileage columns are blank for most vehicles in most years
(@tbl-dd-mileage), simply because a vehicle is on the road for only part of
the period. A fairer measure is the share of the vehicles on the road in a
year, that is with a `pca_YYYY` that is not `unborn` or `dead`, that have a
mileage for that year (@fig-dd-mileage).

On that measure about `r yr(2015, "share_mileage")` of vehicles on the
road have a mileage in each year from 2010 to 2023. The rest are mostly
vehicles not yet due their first MOT, and vehicles in the years after their
last test whose status is still `unknown`. Coverage is higher in the first
years (`r yr(min(by_year$year), "share_mileage")` in `r min(by_year$year)`)
and falls in the last two, to `r yr(2024, "share_mileage")` in 2024 and
`r yr(2025, "share_mileage")` in 2025, because many vehicles have not yet had
the test that closes the year.

Of the mileages present, almost all are judged plausible: the share flagged
implausible is at most `r fmt_pct(max(mc$n_not_legit / mc$n_with_mileage), 1)`
in any year. `total_mileage` is never blank, but is 0 for vehicles with no mileage in any
year.

`odometer_est_YYYY` is present in each year for as many vehicles as have a
plausible mileage (`r yr(2015, "share_odometer")` of those on the road in
2015), so it adds no years that `mileage_YYYY` does not already cover.

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-mileage
#| fig-cap: "Share of the vehicles on the road in each year that have a mileage for that year."
#| fig-height: 3
ggplot(by_year, aes(year, share_mileage)) +
  geom_line(colour = cars_cols[1], linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(colour = cars_cols[1], size = 1.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Vehicles on the road with a mileage") +
  theme_cars()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-mileage-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Vehicles on the road in each year, and the share with a mileage, with a plausible mileage and with an estimated odometer reading."
out <- data.frame(
  Year = by_year$year,
  `On the road` = fmt_n(by_year$n_on_road),
  `With a mileage` = fmt_pct(by_year$share_mileage),
  `Plausible, of those with a mileage` = fmt_pct(by_year$share_legit),
  `With an odometer estimate` = fmt_pct(by_year$share_odometer),
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(out, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, for each year. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("mileage"))
```
